references.text: David asks for God's guidance to avoid falling into temptation, which reflects Jesus' call to pray so as not to give in to temptation.
Isaiah speaks of the strength that comes from the Lord, which can help believers overcome weakness, paralleling Jesus' words about the spirit being willing but the flesh weak.
Mark repeats Jesus' exhortation to be watchful and pray to avoid temptation, which directly mirrors the message in Matthew.
Luke includes a similar event where Jesus prays in Gethsemane and emphasizes the importance of prayer to resist temptations.
John highlights Jesus' prayer that his disciples would not fall into the world's temptations, which resonates with his exhortation in Matthew.

Hebrews speaks of Jesus as our high priest who can sympathize with our weaknesses and encourages us to approach God's throne with confidence to receive grace, reflecting the need to pray to avoid temptation.
James discusses temptations and how they come from our own desires, which underscores Jesus' point about the weakness of the flesh.
Peter urges believers to be sober and watchful because the devil is like a roaring lion, mirroring Jesus' warning to stay alert and pray.
